messages.subject: Initial values or basic logic problem. Or both.
parts:
Hi,

I have a model running in which I generate the expected number subclinical cases per year of a disease from a random walk process, then manipulate those values along with some other parameters and input data to get expected numbers of clinical cases and then expected number of diagnoses. The observed data are diagnosis counts per year, D[y] ~ Poisson(exp_D[y]). Samples for the numbers of subclinical, clinical and diagnosed cases are created in the generated quantities section.

This seems to be working. However, I would now like to move away from the random walk for expected number of new subclinical cases so that this would be a function of the number of infectious individuals (the total number of clinical cases that had not yet been diagnosed - assuming diagnosis => treatment => no further transmission). In this way, a period of putting high effort into diagnosis and treatment would result in a reduction in the size of the pool of infective individuals and less new subclinical cases.

In my running model, I supply initial values for the expected number of subclinical cases per year, along with all my other parameters, and the random walk for the expected number subclinical cases per year is in the model section:

model{
 exp_subclinical[1] ~ gamma(esc1,1);
 for( oy in 2:n_years ){
   exp_subclinical[oy] ~ gamma(exp_subclinical[oy-1],1);
 }
/*
 ...
 some other parameter sampling statements
 exp_clinical and exp_diag calculated in transformed parameters section
 ...
*/
 for( dy in 1:n_obs_diag_years ){
  obs_diag[ dy ] ~ poisson( exp_diag[ year_obs_diag[ dy ] ] );
 }
}


In my revised model, the expected subclinical cases are being calculated in the transformed parameter section:

transformed parameters {
 real exp_subclinical[n_years];
 real exp_clinical[n_years];
 real exp_diag[n_years];
 real exp_infective_pool[n_years];


 for( iy in 1:n_years){
  exp_subclinical[iy] <-
   r[r_period[iy]]*exp_infective_pool[iy];
 }
/*
 ...
 various calculations resulting in exp_clinical and exp_diag
 ...
*/
{
  real cumc[n_years];
  real cumd[n_years];
  cumc <- cumulative_sum( exp_clinical );
  cumd <- cumulative_sum( exp_diag );
  exp_infective_pool[1] <- 0;
  for( y in 2:n_years ){
    exp_infective_pool[y] <- cumc[y-1]-cumd[y-1];
  }
 }
}


The code compiles, but from my rstan run I get:

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'xx' NOW (CHAIN 1).
[1] "Error : Rejecting initial value:"
[2] "  Log probability evaluates to log(0), i.e. negative infinity."
[3] "  Stan can't start sampling from this initial value."
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done


I've tried supplying initial values for exp_subclinical and/or exp_infective_pool, with the same error.

Is my problem purely one of getting sensible initial values? And if so, on which transformed parameter(s)?

Or is there something wrong with what I am trying to do?

Thanks,
Ron.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Initial values or basic logic problem. Or both.
parts:
On Thursday, February 18, 2016 at 8:57:43 AM UTC-5, Ron wrote:
I've tried supplying initial values for exp_subclinical and/or exp_infective_pool, with the same error.

Is my problem purely one of getting sensible initial values? And if so, on which transformed parameter(s)?

Or is there something wrong with what I am trying to do?

Good initial values are only rarely necessary. And you can't supply initial values on transformed parameters because they are just derived from the initial values of the parameters. I would put a
print("log-posterior = ", get_lp());
before and after every statement in the model block involving ~ or increment_log_prob() to see where it starts to underflow. These Poisson models can be prone to numerical problems and it is usually best to use the
~ poisson_log(alpha);
parameterization described in section 40.6 of the Stan User manual, which allows you to keep everything in log-units.

Ben

I have a feedback loop where exp_subclinical = function_of(exp_infected_pool, other) ===> exp_clinical = function_of(exp_subclinical, other vars) ===> exp_diag = function_of(exp_clinical,other vars) ===> exp_infected_pool=cumsum(exp_clinical)-cumsum(exp_diag) ===> exp_subclinical= function_of(exp_infected_pool, other).

Is there some way I can initialise exp_subclinical, say:

if( iteration == 1){
 exp_subclinical <- some_values_supplied;
} else {
 exp_subclinical <- function_of(exp_infected_pool);
}


Ron.

Hi Bob,

Sorry for the delay in replying.

Can you include your whole model rather than just pieces of
it?  It's hard to guess what the rest is.

Here it is:
data {
 int<lower=1> n_obs_years;
 int<lower=1> n_obs_diag_years;
 int<lower=0> n_pre_obs_years;
 int<lower=n_obs_years> n_years;
 int<lower=1> n_effort_parm;
 int<lower=0> obs_diag[n_obs_diag_years];
 int<lower=1> year_obs_diag[n_obs_diag_years];
 int<lower=1,upper=n_effort_parm> effort_level[n_years];
 int<lower=1> n_q;
 int<lower=1,upper=n_q> q_level[n_years];
 real ipd_shape;
 real ipd_rate;
 real ddd_shape;
 real ddd_rate;
 real over_disp;
}

transformed data {
 real rev_ipd[n_years];
 real ipd_hazard[n_years];
 real ddd_hazard[n_years];
 real max_effort;
 real esc1;
 {
  int j;
  for( i in 1:n_years ){
   j <- n_years-i+1;
   rev_ipd[i] <- gamma_cdf( j, ipd_shape, ipd_rate )-
                 gamma_cdf( j-1, ipd_shape, ipd_rate );
   ipd_hazard[i] <- ( gamma_cdf( i, ipd_shape, ipd_rate )-
                      gamma_cdf( i-1, ipd_shape, ipd_rate ) )/
                    ( 1 - gamma_cdf( i-1, ipd_shape, ipd_rate ) );
   ddd_hazard[i] <- ( gamma_cdf( i, ddd_shape, ddd_rate )-
                      gamma_cdf( i-1, ddd_shape, ddd_rate ) )/
                    ( 1 - gamma_cdf( i-1, ddd_shape, ddd_rate ) );
  }
 }
 max_effort <- 0.99/max(ddd_hazard) ;
 esc1 <- max(obs_diag);
}

parameters {
 real<lower=0.01,upper=max_effort> effort[n_effort_parm];
 real<lower=0> q[n_q];
 real<lower=1> inf_pool_1;

}

transformed parameters {
 real exp_subclinical[n_years];
 real exp_clinical[n_years];
 real exp_diag[n_years];
 real exp_infective_pool[n_years];

for( dy in 1:n_years ){
  exp_subclinical[dy] <- q[q_level[dy]]*exp_infective_pool[dy]; 
  exp_diag[dy] <- 0;
 }
 for( oy in 1:n_years ){
   real subc[oy];
   real subipd[oy];
   real left;
   real edy;
   int dy;
   subc <- head( exp_subclinical, oy );
   subipd <- segment(rev_ipd,n_years-oy+1,oy);
   exp_clinical[oy] <- dot_product( subc, subipd );
   left <- exp_clinical[oy];
   dy <- oy;
   while( dy < n_years+1 && left  > 0 ){
     edy <- ddd_hazard[dy-oy+1]*effort[effort_level[dy]]*left;
     exp_diag[dy] <- exp_diag[dy]+edy;
     left <- left-edy;
     dy <- dy+1;

}
 }
 {
  real cumc[n_years];
  real cumd[n_years];
  cumc <- cumulative_sum( exp_clinical );
  cumd <- cumulative_sum( exp_diag );
exp_infective_pool[1] <- inf_pool_1;

for( y in 2:n_years ){
    exp_infective_pool[y] <- cumc[y-1]-cumd[y-1];
  }
 }
}

model {
 inf_pool_1 ~ gamma(esc1/(1+over_disp),1/(1+over_disp));
 for( j in 1:n_effort_parm ){
   effort[j] ~ normal(1,0.25)T[0.01,max_effort] ;
 }
 for( j in 1:n_q ){
  q[j] ~ gamma(10,9);

}
 for( dy in 1:n_obs_diag_years ){
  obs_diag[ dy ] ~ poisson( exp_diag[ year_obs_diag[ dy ] ] );
 }
}

generated quantities {
 int subclinical[n_years];
 int clinical[n_years];
 int diagnosed[n_years];
 for( yr in 1:n_years ){
  clinical[yr]  <- 0;
  diagnosed[yr] <- 0;
 }
 {
  int left;
  int n;
  int dy;
  {
   int oy;
   for( iy in 1:n_years ){
    subclinical[iy] <- neg_binomial_2_rng( exp_subclinical[iy], exp_subclinical[iy]/over_disp );
    left <- subclinical[iy];
    oy <- iy;
    while( oy < n_years+1 && left  > 0 ){
      n <- binomial_rng( left, ipd_hazard[oy-iy+1] );
      clinical[oy] <- clinical[oy]+n;
      left <- left-n;
      oy <- oy+1;
    }
   }
  }
  for( oy in 1:n_years ){
   left <- clinical[oy];
   dy <- oy;
   while( dy < n_years+1 && left  > 0 ){
     n <- binomial_rng( left, ddd_hazard[dy-oy+1]*effort[ effort_level[dy] ] );
     diagnosed[dy] <- diagnosed[dy]+n;
     left <- left-n;
     dy <- dy+1;
   }
  }
 }
}

Parameters and data will always have valid values assigned
from the outside.  Every other variable has to be defined
before it is used.

I think this is my main problem because exp_subclinical and exp_infective_pool are dependent on one another and I can't supply a set of initial values for either.

Ron

> I think this is my main problem because exp_subclinical and exp_infective_pool are dependent on one another and I can't supply a set of initial values for either.

This is indeed a problem. At this point, exp_infective_pool[dy]
is not defined. I'm not sure what you expected Stan to do here.
It's just like any other programming language --- it just executes
the statements in the order they arise. Can you define exp_infective_pool
first? Then you can just define exp_subclinical later as:

exp_subclinical <- q[q_level] .* exp_infect_pool;

- Bob
